newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends lower on exports, Sparks estimate.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends lower on exports, Sparks estimate.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed lower on bearish input from the export sector with a prediction from the CEO of Sparks Companies also cited, traders said.
"It's being pressured by the fact that nearby export business is not coming from U.S.-origin," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.

News Egypt bought 200,000 tonnes of wheat from Argentina and 300,000 from Australia was cited. Traders said the deals were not surprising but again did remind the market of the lethargic pace of U.S. wheat export sales. "The surprise would have been if they had bought from us," a trader said.
Also USDA early Monday said U.S. wheat export inspections for the week ended December 5 totaled 12.517 million bushels, below the low end of trade expectations for 13 to 16 million bushels.

Nearby December showed some buoyancy because that month is lightly traded and nearing expiration at 1201 CST December 19. Support under the December also came from perceptions the light deliveries posted on that contract again were stopped by U.S. mills.
Wheat closed one to 5-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with December down one at $3.90.
Traders said news coming from a Kansas City meeting of the National Grain and Feed Association also weighed on the markets, including wheat.

The CEO of Memphis-based analytical firm Sparks Companies Monday said the U.S. 1996 corn crop would total 9.3 to 9.4 billion bushels, above USDA's November outlook for 9.265 billion. Carrol Brunthaver also said CBOT July wheat futures would trade below $3.00 per bushel during harvest next summer.
CBOT July wheat closed Monday at $3.30-1/2 per bushel, down 2-1/2 cents.
SAK Futures, O'Connor and Co and LIT America each sold one million bushels of March, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 10,000 contracts, below the 10,991 traded Friday, according to the CBOT.
In wheat options, Smith Barney bought 75 July $3.40 puts at 23-1/2, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 2,700 contracts, above the 2,663 traded Friday.
